code:
# BAD
assert run("debug-env") == "{'x': 1, 'y': 2}"

# GOOD, parse the output and compare as a set of pairs
result = run("debug-env")
pairs  = set(result.strip("{}").split(", "))
assert pairs == {"'x': 1", "'y': 2"}
description: A raw-string comparison that depends on pair order, and a set-of-pairs comparison that ignores order.

steps.description: This shows how to compare an environment display. The page says not to compare the raw string, because the pair order can be semantically arbitrary even though Python 3.7+ preserves insertion order.
The `BAD` line compares the whole string `"{'x': 1, 'y': 2}"` at once, which depends on the order of the pairs.
The `GOOD` version runs `debug-env`, strips the braces, splits on `", "` into pairs, and compares the set of pairs. A set ignores order, so the test passes whatever order the pairs come in.

title: Comparing Environment Display
